nodes.name: Hydrothermal corrosion
nodes.procedure: Newly washed stainless steel plate is converted into corroded stainless steel plate (SPN) by a facile hydrothermal treatment in ammonium solution. Along with this process, the color of the stainless steel plate is changed from grey to olive, indicating the successful growth of the rusty layer.
nodes.source_text: newly washed stainless steel plate is converted into corroded stainless steel plate (SPN) by a facile hydrothermal treatment in ammonium solution.

nodes.name: EORC activation of corroded plate
nodes.procedure: Electrochemical oxidation-reduction cycling of corroded stainless steel plate is undertaken to synthesize EORC-activated rusty stainless steel plate (SPN50) in 1 M KOH solution. Varisized particles are densely grown on the surface, accompanied with the decrease of average size (122 nm) and rougher surfaces due to the in situ partial consumption of the smooth particle and growth of hierarchical nanosheets along its surface via EORC.
nodes.source_text: electrochemical oxidation-reduction cycling of corroded stainless steel plate is undertaken to synthesize EORC-activated rusty stainless steel plate (SPN50) in 1 M KOH solution.

nodes.name: Direct EORC activation
nodes.procedure: The stainless steel plate, treated with EORC, denoted as SP50, is also endowed with dense cross-linked Fe/(Ni)OOH nanosheets on the surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM images show close-packed uneven particles with average size of 175 nm on corroded stainless steel plate surface, quite different from smooth stainless steel plate surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As the atom force microscopy (AFM) images and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images displayed, the surface of the corroded stainless steel plate is close-packed with uneven particles with average size of 175 nm, quite different from the smooth surface of stainless steel plate.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows varisized particles densely grown on EORC-activated rusty stainless steel plate surface with average size 122 nm and rougher surfaces compared to corroded stainless steel plate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1f and Figure S1, varisized particles are densely grown on the surface of EORC-activated rusty stainless steel plate, in accompany with the decrease of average size (122 nm) and rougher surfaces in comparison with those of corroded stainless steel plate.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals interconnected nanosheets on particles of EORC-activated rusty stainless steel plate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: And the TEM images of EORC-activated rusty stainless steel plate further reveal the successful formation interconnected nanosheet on the particles (Figure 1i).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows distinct lattice spacing (0.22, 0.25, and 0.268 nm) indexed to (101) plane of (Ni₀.₆₇Fe₀.₃₃)OOH, (211) and (400) plane of FeOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Accordingly, the HRTEM images show that distinct lattice spacing (0.22, 0.25, and 0.268 nm) is indexed to (101) plane of (Ni₀.₆₇Fe₀.₃₃)OOH, (211) and (400) plane of FeOOH, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM confirms rough surface of particles on EORC-activated rusty stainless steel plate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HAADF-STEM image of EORC-activated rusty stainless steel plate further confirms the rough surface of the particles, in accordance with SEM results (Figure 2a,f).

nodes.characterization_summary: Element mapping shows Fe, Ni, and O homogeneously distributed on particle/nanosheet structure of EORC-activated rusty stainless steel plate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: And the corresponding element mapping images (Figure 2b-d, S4 and S5) show that Fe, Ni, and O are homogeneously distributed on the overall particle/nanosheet structure of EORC-activated stainless steel plate, corroded stainless steel plate and EORC-activated rusty stainless steel plate.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms presence of Fe, Ni, Cr, O; Fe 2p3/2 peaks at 706.5 eV (Fe), 709.8 eV (FeO), 710.6 eV (Fe2O3), 711.5 eV (FeOOH); Ni 2p3/2 peaks at 852.6 eV (Ni), 854.7 eV (NiO), 855.5 eV (NiOOH/Ni(OH)2); O 1s peaks at 529.7 eV (O2-), 531 eV (OH-), 531.8 eV (H2O); higher FeOOH and NiOOH contents and higher OH- percentage in SPN50.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence of Fe, Ni, Cr, and O is confirmed by the survey spectra (Figure S6 and Table S1). And the high resolution Fe2p3/2 spectra can be deconvoluted into four types, assigned to Fe (706.5 eV), FeO (709.8 eV), Fe2O3 (710.6 eV), and FeOOH (711.5 eV, Figure 2h). As for Ni 2p3/2, three fitted peaks located at 852.6, 854.7 and 855.5 eV are ascribed to metallic Ni, NiO, and NiOOH/Ni(OH)2 respectively... Moreover, higher contents of FeOOH and NiOOH are harvested by EORC-activated rusty stainless steel plate... The fitted peaks of the O1s spectrum corresponded to O2- (529.7 eV) OH- (531 eV), and physical adsorption of water (H2O, 531.8 eV) respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EORC-activated rusty stainless steel plate has smallest average contact angle (0°) compared to corroded stainless steel plate (19.2°), EORC-activated stainless steel plate (13.2°), and stainless steel plate (78.1°).
nodes.evidence_snippet: EORC-activated rusty stainless steel plate has the smallest average contact angle (0°) in comparison with corroded stainless steel plate (19.2°), EORC-activated stainless steel plate (13.2°), and stainless steel plate (78.1°).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns identify particles mainly consist of Fe/(Ni) oxide/hydroxide.
nodes.evidence_snippet: And the XRD pattern and Raman spectra identify that the particles are mainly consisted of Fe/(Ni) oxide/hydroxide (Figure S2-3).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra verify superficial nanosheets mainly composed of Fe/(Ni)OOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As the Raman spectra and XRD patterns further verified, the superficial nanosheets induced by EORC are mainly composed of Fe/(Ni)OOH (Figure S2-3).

nodes.characterization_summary: Electron resistivity of SPN50, SP50, SPN, and SP are all low at 0.07-0.08 mΩ cm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Remarkably, the electron resistivity of corroded stainless steel plate and EORC-activated stainless steel plate are low (0.07 and 0.08 mΩ cm) albeit with the growth of various particles, respectively, completely inheriting the high conductivity of SP (0.07 mΩ cm).
